Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a prominent, tortuous vascular structure in the right lower zone, which, combined with the clinical history of haemoptysis in a young adult, is characteristic of a pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (PAVM). PAVMs typically present as well-defined nodular or serpiginous opacities representing dilated feeding arteries and draining veins, distinguishing them from the systemic arterial supply seen in sequestration or the diffuse patterns of infection/heart failure.
